claims.claim: Reviewers report that visual effects and flashing screen elements cause severe motion sickness and eye strain.

citations.review_text:
I love rhythm games, and I really enjoyed this one, but WTF... there are SUPER DUPER too many effects. My eyes pls. 😂 I don't know if it's motion sickness or what, but it was so overwhelming.

It would be great if there were an option to reduce or disable some of the visual effects. I think it would make the game much more enjoyable and accessible for players who are sensitive to all the flashing and screen effects.

I wanted to like Muse Dash; however, this game gives me severe motion sickness that I've never experienced before in the 20+ years that I've been playing rhythm games. This isn't a problem on very slow songs and difficulties where comparatively not much on-screen movement is happening, but those are more or less "training" levels and are well below the BPM/difficulty I'm used to playing rhythm games at (meaning: it's boring). 

For reference, I'm used to sitting at my PC for hours on end playing Osu! with little to no issue. So, I was surprised that within 30 seconds of a random song on Muse Dash, the on-screen effects became so overwhelming that it hurt to look at my screen and I began to feel ill. 

Unfortunately, the only display setting that can be adjusted is the in-game background brightness, and this does basically nothing to help with the issue. I wish there were at least settings available to toggle some of the visual effects, bobbing, shaking, etc., because otherwise it is unplayable for me. 

Anyways - game cute, waifus pretty, but avoid if you have any concerns about motion sickness.
songs are all p2w 💔 anyway I'm still overstim bc of this game

claims.claim: Reviewers note that the game features a two-button control scheme which makes it easy to learn and read compared to other rhythm games, though higher difficulties become extremely challenging.

citations.review_text:
10/10, one of the best rhythm games out there.
I've been playing this game since around 2018, sticking with the mobile version until recently, and the fun hasn't changed one bit. The bigger and clearer screen is a huge improvement, especially since your fingers don't cover the sides of the screen like they do on mobile. Simple mechanics, an awesome selection of songs (even though some are locked behind DLC, and some collab content is gone because of that January tragedy...), cute and cool art style, and eye-catching animations, pretty much every aspect is top-notch.

The mechanics are somewhat similar to Taiko no Tatsujin, but simpler. Instead of having all the notes cluttered in the middle, they're divided between two lanes, which makes things much easier to read. That said, the note patterns in the higher-star difficulties can be absolutely evil... and yet, I love it.

I also discovered a lot of artists through this game whose music I ended up falling in love with after listening to more of their songs. So, in a way, I'm pretty thankful to this game for introducing me to them.

I've seen some people complain in the reviews about the suggestive art and call it "goonslop." Well... that's kind of one of the selling points of the game. Cry about it.
Overall, it's a solid, cute-themed rhythm game with simple mechanics, cute girls, and mostly cute songs. I'd recommend it if you don't really mind the suggestive art style the game goes for.

Actually, even if you don't like rythm game but like good music get this game. I discovered great music thanks to this game, it's tons of collabs and just great composers it has. It is simply a 18/10 for me

Some of the music I don't like but, the game is fun. I will say this game got me into another rhythm game which is unbeatable which is a lot like this game but more mechanics but less dlc at the moment. Play Muse Dash its like $3 and plus dlc is huge its got hours of content to explore in the dlc.

muse dash is one of my all time favorite rhythm games. i genuinely think that you won't find an easier to read rhythm game out there, despite how complex it appears at first. there are soo many fun charts and some of the most enjoyable gimmick maps i've seen in any rhythm game (overlapping notes and sliders mostly). just buy the base game when it's on sale and check it out, if you enjoy it, get the dlc. such a fun game, couldn't recommend more.

Muse Dash is basically what happens if a rhythm game and an anime fever dream had a baby.

You press a few buttons, everything looks cute and harmless… and then suddenly the screen turns into pure chaos and you’re just praying your fingers are still attached to your brain.

I went in thinking “this looks easy.”

I was wrong. Very confidently wrong. (atleast on the highest difficulties)

Still, it’s super addictive. You fail, you cry, you immediately hit retry like you didn’t just get emotionally humbled by a song with cute visuals and zero mercy.

Music slaps, visuals are adorable, and my dignity slowly disappears with every track.

10/10 would get destroyed again.

Muse Dash is fantastic rhythm game. It has many nice soundtracks, unique gameplay, and engaging character mechanics. It’s very welcoming to newcomers but scales beautifully, offering some genuinely tough challenges on higher difficulties. It is also often updated and makes collabs with other games, artists, etc.

However, before buying, you should keep in mind, that base game is just a gateway! Most of actual content is locked behind DLC. It is a one-time purchase that covers all future updates, but cost can be high for some. If you aren't planning to buy DLC, you're better off checking out alternatives like Audiosurf 1 & 2 or Beat Hazard 1-3.

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the game as easy to learn with difficulties scaling up to very challenging charts for advanced players.

citations.review_text:
It's literally 0.53 cents as I'm writing this review, dear lord get this game.
It's colorful, it's cheery, it's upbeat, it's fun. You're allowed to feel yourself whenever you beat a stage.
I'm not into anime art style, but I think there's a little something for everyone in this game (not a fan of the slightly suggestive stuff).
The DLC pack isn't necessary, but you're missing out on a lot of great tracks, cool stage moments and snazzy characters/ways to play the game.
Whether you want something chill and relaxing to play, or a terrifyingly demanding and challenging game to push you, this sleeper hit does it all.

(Took me 5 years to earn the April Fool's achievement because I kept missing the date each year)

One of the most comfortable rhythm games I’ve ever tried. It has a large selection of songs (and it keeps growing with updates), plenty of collaborations (with indie artists and producers, vocaloid, as well as well-known gacha game IPs like Arknights, Blue Archive, and Wuthering Waves), and a wide range of difficulties (easy for beginners who are just learning, casual levels, all the way up to ultra-hard charts for pros).

The downside is that to fully enjoy the game, you need to buy the Muse Plus DLC to access all the music (the free selection is very limited, and honestly, many of the best stages are only available through the DLC), along with a few additional minor benefits.
